title: Add 7-day Dependabot cooldown
description: Add a 7-day cooldown to the Dependabot GitHub Actions update config. This prevents Dependabot from immediately pulling newly released dependency versions, reducing supply-chain risk from opportunistic package compromises and stability risk from regressions in new releases.

title: Organize extending examples by product and image
description:
Reorganizes `extending/` into product/image subfolders and adds per-product decision-guide READMEs. The flat example list made it hard to answer "which image do I customize for this goal?" The directory structure now answers that question directly.

New structure: `workbench/server/`, `workbench/session/`, `workbench/session-init/`, `connect/server/`, `connect/content/`, `package-manager/server/`.

New examples (previously no examples existed for the images where users' sessions and deployed content actually run):

- `workbench/session/r-python-packages` — pre-install R and Python packages in a session image
- `workbench/session/system-dependencies` — install system libs for session packages
- `workbench/session-init` — multi-stage bake for a self-contained session image (no runtime init container needed)
- `workbench/server/config` — apply a custom Workbench server configuration file
- `connect/content/r-python-packages` — pre-install R and Python packages in a content image
- `connect/content/system-dependencies` — install system libs for content packages

Also fixes the CI matrix job names to use the relative path under `extending/` (e.g. `workbench/session/system-dependencies` instead of `system-dependencies`), preventing duplicate job names now that `system-dependencies` exists in both `workbench/session/` and `connect/content/`.

This PR must land before the two product-repo PRs that link to these paths:

- https://github.com/posit-dev/images-workbench/pull/114
- https://github.com/posit-dev/images-connect/pull/210

title: Remove --quiet from quarto tinytex install command
description:
The `--quiet` flag suppresses `quarto install tinytex` output,
including the actual error message when the install fails. Recent
CI flakes related to GitHub API rate limits during the install were
nearly impossible to diagnose because of this.

Directly edit the rendered Containerfile to drop `--quiet`. The
upstream template fix lives in:

- https://github.com/posit-dev/images-shared/pull/546

title: Add fleet example for customized Posit product images
description:
Adds `extending/posit-team/`, a worked example of a team managing a
fleet of customized Posit Workbench, Posit Connect, and Posit Package
Manager images on top of the official Minimal bases. The existing
`extending/` examples each cover one customization of one image. This
one shows the same pattern at fleet scale, using Bakery to render and
tag a set of images consistently.

The example lives under `extending/` rather than `bakery/` because the
use case is customization, not learning Bakery itself. The rendered
Containerfiles are committed alongside the templates, so building does
not require Bakery: `docker build` works directly.

`extending.yaml` is updated to handle both plain and Bakery-managed
extending examples in one workflow.

title: Install Quarto from the Posit Open apt repo in 06-matrix-images
description:
## Summary

Supersedes #18.

Replaces the Quarto tarball download in `bakery/06-matrix-images` with an apt install from the [Posit Open apt repo](https://dl.posit.co/public/open/). This avoids the root cause of #18's failing CI — the final build stage did not declare `ARG TARGETARCH`, so the substituted URL expanded to `...-linux-.tar.gz` and returned 404.

## Why apt instead of fixing the tarball URL

- `quarto` is a multi-arch deb (amd64 + arm64) available on both `jammy` and `noble` in the Posit Open repo, so the install works uniformly without URL construction or `TARGETARCH` handling.
- The base image already runs `setup.deb.sh` for the Pro repo; adding the Open repo is one symmetrical line of the same pattern.
- No tarball extraction, no GitHub release mirror dependency.

## Notable side effects

- **Install path changed.** The `quarto` deb installs the binary at `/opt/quarto/bin/quarto` and symlinks it into `/usr/local/bin/quarto` via the package's postinst script. There is no longer a `/opt/quarto/${QUARTO_VERSION}/` version-scoped directory.
- **TinyTeX install.** Invoked as `/opt/quarto/bin/quarto install tinytex --no-prompt --quiet`. `xz-utils` is installed explicitly because the TinyTeX tarball is `.tar.xz` and the Ubuntu 24.04 base image does not include it.
- **Goss tests updated.** Now assert `package.quarto.versions == ${QUARTO_VERSION}` (dpkg-authoritative) and `file: /opt/quarto/bin/quarto` instead of the old `/opt/quarto/${QUARTO_VERSION}` path check.

## Test plan

- [x] `bakery update files` regenerates the rendered Containerfile + goss yaml cleanly (verified locally)
- [x] `docker buildx build --build-arg R_VERSION=4.4.3 --build-arg PYTHON_VERSION=3.13.13 --build-arg QUARTO_VERSION=1.9.37 ...` succeeds
- [x] `quarto --version` → `1.9.37` in the built image
- [x] `dgoss run` passes all 8 tests (`Count: 8, Failed: 0, Skipped: 0`)
- [x] CI (`Examples - Bakery / Build and test - 06-matrix-images`) passes

title: Add pro-drivers and quarto extending examples
description:
## Summary

Adds two new `extending/` examples demonstrating how to layer commonly needed components on top of the Minimal product images.

- **`pro-drivers/`** — Installs the Posit Pro Drivers (`rstudio-drivers`) on a Workbench `-min` image. The Posit apt repository is already configured in the base image, so the package can be installed directly. Copies the sample `odbcinst.ini` into `/etc/` so the drivers are registered with unixODBC, matching the pattern used by the rendered Connect Standard image.
- **`quarto/`** — Installs Quarto and TinyTeX on a Connect `-min` image. Quarto is downloaded from the official GitHub release and symlinked into `/usr/local/bin`. TinyTeX is installed via `quarto install tinytex`, which ships a fuller set of LaTeX packages than the standalone TinyTeX installer. `xz-utils` is installed explicitly because the `-min` image does not include it and the TinyTeX archive is `.tar.xz`.

Both patterns mirror the rendered `.std` Containerfiles in the sibling product repos:
- Pro drivers: [`images-connect/.../Containerfile.ubuntu2204.std`](https://github.com/posit-dev/images-connect/blob/main/connect/2025.07/Containerfile.ubuntu2204.std), [`images-workbench/.../Containerfile.ubuntu2204.std`](https://github.com/posit-dev/images-workbench/blob/main/workbench/2025.09/Containerfile.ubuntu2204.std)
- Quarto + TinyTeX: [`images-connect/.../Containerfile.ubuntu2204.std`](https://github.com/posit-dev/images-connect/blob/main/connect/2026.03/Containerfile.ubuntu2204.std)

Closes #19.
Closes #20.

## Test plan

- [x] `docker buildx build` succeeds for both examples
- [x] `quarto --version` prints `1.9.36` and `tlmgr --version` reports TeX Live 2026 in the built quarto image
- [x] `/etc/odbcinst.ini` in the built pro-drivers image lists every Pro Driver (Athena, BigQuery, Cassandra, ...)
- [ ] CI (`Examples - Extending`) builds both examples in the matrix

title: Skip cache restore in bakery example matrix job
description:
build-and-test never runs alongside a setup-bakery is-writer job, so
its dependency-version cache restore always misses and logs a
confusing "Artifact not found" error on every run.

Opt out via the new restore-cache input on setup-bakery.

Blocked on the images-shared PR below merging to main -- this
workflow pins setup-bakery@main, and composite actions reject
unrecognized inputs, so CI here will fail until that lands. Opening
as a draft for that reason.

- https://github.com/posit-dev/images-shared/pull/708
- https://github.com/posit-dev/images-shared/issues/686

title: Group dependabot security updates into one PR
description:
Dependabot's `groups` key only covers version updates by default;
security-alert PRs need an explicit `applies-to: security-updates`
group or they arrive individually, ungrouped.

Add a security sibling group to the `actions` group so a future
security alert lands as one grouped PR instead of one per
dependency.
